html:
On 23 November 1733 enslaved Africans on the Danish island of St John rose against their masters, seized the fort at Coral Bay and took control of most of the island. They held out for about six months.

Many of the rebels were Akwamu people from the Gold Coast, once nobles and warriors who had been enslaved after their state fell. Drought, a hurricane and harsh new laws had made life desperate.

The Danes could not defeat them alone and called in French troops from Martinique. In 1734, facing capture, many rebels killed themselves rather than return to slavery. The revolt is remembered in the Virgin Islands as a fight for freedom, and its leaders link the islands to Akan history and the slave trade.
sum: On 23 November 1733 enslaved Africans on the Danish island of St John rose against their masters, seized the fort at Coral Bay and took control of most of the island. They held out for about six months.
